For me, the first problem was that it was incremental. She wasn't crazy in the beginning, or at least not noticeably so. We were caught up in that swirl of emotions at the beginning of a relationship, and it was all fine. It was only later - at the point at which the relationship, as they do, started to settle down into day-to-day routine - that things started going sideways. In hindsight, I presume that the rush of emotion early in the relationship was enough, by itself, to fulfill her need for drama, and it was only later that she had to go out of her way to create it.

From there on out (we were together for about another year after things started to go sour), it was a combination of things.

Part of it was that, naturally, some of the shit she gave me was at least somewhat legitimate. She (and I would assume this is true for most manipulative people) generally didn't just make stuff up out of thin air (that likely wouldn't have worked). When she'd find a "fault" of mine to go to work on, it was generally a real fault that I really possessed, and often one of which I was already well aware. So I'd go along - it really did seem to be my problem, because it really was about my fault(s) that I really did possess.

Later, as I started to realize that this was a pattern of behavior - that she was manipulating me and deliberately undermining me rather than just offering legitimate criticism, I started to work out why she was doing it - I started to note her weakness and fear and self-doubt and how that led her to try to undermine me, and I spent a while trying to get through to her. That, unsurprisingly, didn't work - my attitude started to change then and I was much less likely to respond to her manipulations and much more likely to try to shift the focus to her instead of me, and I'm sure that terrified her. In any event, she then doubled down on the crazy and pulled a lot of really ugly shit in a short time, which actually worked out for me. One night, I just packed my stuff and left.

A sidelight - one advantage that I had near the end - I adopted a stray cat that had been hanging around a gas station up the street, and the cat hated her. I've never seen a cat so obviously hate a specific person before. And it was really quite nice to have someone on my side.
